en: 'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-'Azim al-'Anbari and Ahmad ibn Ja'far al-Ma'qiri narrated to me; they said: al-Nadr—who is Ibn Muhammad al-Yamami—narrated to us: 'Ikrimah narrated to us: Abu Zumayl narrated to us: Ibn 'Abbas narrated to me, saying: The Muslims used not to look at Abu Sufyan nor sit with him. So he said to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): 'O Prophet of Allah, three things—grant them to me.' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'I have the best and most beautiful of Arab women, Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan; I will marry her to you.' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'And Mu'awiyah—make him a scribe before you.' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'And appoint me as a commander so that I may fight the disbelievers just as I used to fight the Muslims.' He said: 'Yes.' Abu Zumayl said: Had he not asked that of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), he would not have granted it to him, because he was never asked for anything except that he said: 'Yes.'

Abu 'Amir al-Ash'ari and Abu Kuraib both narrated to us from Abu Usamah; Abu 'Amir said: Abu Usamah narrated to us: Burayd ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Burdah narrated to me, from his grandfather Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Indeed, when the Ash'aris run short of provisions during military expeditions or the food of their families runs low in Medina, they collect whatever they have in a single cloth, then divide it among themselves in one vessel equally. Thus they are of me and I am of them.'

Abu Kuraib Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us: Burayd narrated to us, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Indeed, I recognize the voices of the group of Ash'aris reciting the Quran when they enter at night, and I recognize their dwellings from their voices reciting the Quran by night, even though I did not see their dwellings when they camped by day. And among them is a wise man who, when he meets the cavalry—or he said: the enemy—says to them: "My companions bid you to wait for them."'

'Abdullah ibn Barrad Abu 'Amir al-Ash'ari and Abu Kuraib Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us—and the wording is Abu 'Amir's; they said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Burayd, from Abu Burdah, from his father, who said: When the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) finished with Hunayn, he sent Abu 'Amir in charge of an army to Awtas. He encountered Durayd ibn al-Simmah, and Durayd was killed, and Allah defeated his companions. Abu Musa said: And he sent me along with Abu 'Amir. He said: Abu 'Amir was shot in his knee; a man from Banu Jusham shot him with an arrow that lodged firmly in his knee. I reached him and said: 'O uncle, who shot you?' Abu 'Amir pointed him out to Abu Musa and said: 'That is my killer; do you see him? That is the one who shot me.' Abu Musa said: So I headed straight toward him, pursuing him intently, and caught up with him. When he saw me, he turned away fleeing, so I followed him and began shouting to him: 'Have you no shame? Are you not an Arab? Will you not stand firm?' So he stopped, and he and I clashed and exchanged two blows; I struck him with the sword and killed him. Then I returned to Abu 'Amir and said: 'Indeed, Allah has killed your opponent.' He said: 'Pull out this arrow.' So I pulled it out, and pus/fluid spurted from it. He said: 'O nephew, go to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), convey my greetings of peace to him, and tell him: Abu 'Amir says to you: Seek forgiveness for me.' He said: Abu 'Amir put me in command of the people, survived a short while, and then died. When I returned to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), I entered upon him while he was in a room upon a woven corded bed with a mattress over it, and the cords of the bed had left marks on the back and flanks of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). I informed him of our news and the news of Abu 'Amir, and said to him: 'He said: Tell him to seek forgiveness for me.' The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) called for water, performed ablution with it, raised his hands, and said: 'O Allah, forgive 'Ubayd, Abu 'Amir,' until I saw the whiteness of his armpits. Then he said: 'O Allah, make him on the Day of Resurrection above many of Your creation—or of mankind.' I said: 'And for me, O Messenger of Allah, seek forgiveness!' So the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'O Allah, forgive 'Abdullah ibn Qays his sin, and admit him on the Day of Resurrection to an honorable entrance.' Abu Burdah said: One prayer was for Abu 'Amir and the other for Abu Musa.

Abu 'Amir al-Ash'ari and Abu Kuraib both narrated to us from Abu Usamah; Abu 'Amir said: Abu Usamah narrated to us: Burayd narrated to us, from his grandfather Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, who said: I was with the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) while he was camped at al-Ji'ranah between Mecca and Medina, and Bilal was with him. A bedouin man came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: 'Will you not fulfill for me, O Muhammad, what you promised me?' The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to him: 'Receive glad tidings.' The bedouin said to him: 'You have said "receive glad tidings" to me too many times!' So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) turned to Abu Musa and Bilal like one angry, and said: 'This man has rejected the glad tidings, so accept them you two!' They said: 'We accept, O Messenger of Allah.' Then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) called for a bowl containing water, washed his hands and face in it, spat into it, and said: 'Drink from it and pour some over your faces and upper chests, and receive glad tidings.' So they took the bowl and did what the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had commanded them. Then Umm Salamah called out to them from behind the curtain: 'Save some for your mother from what is in your vessel!' So they saved some of it for her.

Harun ibn 'Abdullah narrated to me: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj said: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah saying: Umm Mubashshir informed me that she heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying in the presence of Hafsah: 'None of the companions of the Tree—those who pledged allegiance under it—shall enter Hellfire, if Allah wills.' She said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He rebuked her, so Hafsah said: {And there is not one of you but will pass over it}. The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, has already said: {Then We will save those who feared Allah and leave the wrongdoers within it, on their knees}.'

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated to us: al-Layth informed us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, that a slave of Hatib came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) complaining of Hatib, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, Hatib will surely enter Hellfire!' Thereupon the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'You have lied; he will not enter it, for he participated in Badr and al-Hudaybiyyah.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us; (H) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Idris informed us; (H) and Rifa'ah ibn al-Haytham al-Wasiti narrated to us: Khalid—meaning Ibn 'Abdullah—narrated to us; all of them from Husayn, from Sa'd ibn 'Ubaydah, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from 'Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) sent me, Abu Marthad al-Ghanawi, and al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam, and all of us were horsemen, saying: 'Go until you reach Rawdat Khakh, for there is a woman from among the polytheists there carrying a letter from Hatib to the polytheists.' And he related with the meaning of the hadith of 'Ubaydullah ibn Abi Rafi' from 'Ali.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Amr al-Naqid, Zuhayr ibn Harb, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us—and the wording is 'Amr's; Ishaq said: 'informed us', and the others said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Amr, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad: 'Ubaydullah ibn Abi Rafi'—who was the scribe of 'Ali—informed me, saying: I heard 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) say: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) sent me, al-Zubayr, and al-Miqdad, saying: 'Go to Rawdat Khakh, for there is a woman traveling in a camel-litter who has a letter, so take it from her.' We set off galloping on our horses until we came upon the woman and said: 'Produce the letter!' She said: 'I have no letter with me.' We said: 'You must produce the letter or you will surely cast off your clothes!' So she produced it from her hair braids. We brought it to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and behold, it was from Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah to some people among the polytheists of Mecca, informing them of some of the affair of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'O Hatib, what is this?' He said: 'Do not be hasty with me, O Messenger of Allah! I was a man attached to Quraysh (Sufyan said: he was an ally to them and not of their blood), while those who were with you among the Emigrants had relatives through whom they protect their families. So since I lacked lineage among them, I wished to do them a favor by which they would protect my relatives. I did not do it out of disbelief or apostasy from my religion, nor out of pleasure with disbelief after Islam.' The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'He has spoken the truth.' 'Umar said: 'Allow me, O Messenger of Allah, to strike the neck of this hypocrite!' He said: 'Indeed, he participated in Badr; and what will make you know? Perhaps Allah looked upon the people of Badr and said: "Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you."' Then Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, revealed: {O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies}. And in the hadith of Abu Bakr and Zuhayr the verse is not mentioned, and Ishaq made it in his narration part of Sufyan's recitation.

Harun ibn Ma'ruf narrated it to us: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated it to us, from Hisham, from his father, who said: Abu Hurayrah used to narrate hadith and say: 'Listen, O lady of the chamber! Listen, O lady of the chamber!' while 'A'ishah was praying. When she finished her prayer, she said to 'Urwah: 'Do you not hear this man and his words just now? The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) would only narrate a hadith such that if a counter were to count it, he could enumerate it.'

Harmalah ibn Yahya al-Tujibi narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, that 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to him that 'A'ishah said: 'Are you not amazed by Abu Hurayrah? He came and sat beside my chamber, narrating from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) making me hear that while I was performing voluntary prayers. Then he stood up before I finished my prayer, and had I caught him, I would have answered back to him: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) did not recite hadiths rapidly one after another as you do.'

'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to us: Abu al-Yaman informed us, from Shu'ayb, from al-Zuhri: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed me that Abu Hurayrah said: 'You say that Abu Hurayrah narrates many hadiths from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)...' similar to their hadith.

Ibn Shihab said: and Ibn al-Musayyab said that Abu Hurayrah said: 'They say: "Abu Hurayrah has narrated too much," and with Allah is the appointed meeting. And they say: "Why is it that the Emigrants and the Ansar do not narrate like his hadiths?" I will tell you about that: my brothers among the Ansar were occupied by working their lands, and my brothers among the Emigrants were occupied by trading in the markets, while I used to remain closely attached to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) for merely my bellyful, witnessing when they were absent and memorizing when they forgot. And one day the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Who among you will spread out his garment and take from this speech of mine, then gather it to his chest, for he will never forget anything he heard?" So I spread out a cloak upon me until he finished his speech, then I gathered it to my chest, and after that day I never forgot anything he narrated to me. Were it not for two verses that Allah revealed in His Book, I would never have narrated anything: {Indeed, those who conceal what We sent down of clear proofs and guidance...} to the end of the two verses.'

'Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Yahya ibn Khalid narrated to me: Ma'n informed us: Malik informed us; (H) and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us; both of them from al-Zuhri, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, with this hadith, except that Malik's narration ended at the conclusion of Abu Hurayrah's statement and did not mention in his hadith the narration from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): 'Whoever spreads out his garment...' to the end of it.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, and Zuhayr ibn Harb all narrated to us from Sufyan; Zuhayr said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from al-A'raj, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: 'You claim that Abu Hurayrah narrates too many hadiths from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and with Allah is the appointed meeting. I was a poor man serving the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) for my bellyful, whereas the Emigrants were occupied by trading in the markets, and the Ansar were occupied by tending to their properties. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever spreads out his garment will never forget anything he hears from me." So I spread out my garment until he finished his speech, then I gathered it to myself, and I never forgot anything I heard from him.'

'Amr al-Naqid narrated to us: 'Umar ibn Yunus al-Yamami narrated to us: 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, from Abu Kathir Yazid ibn 'Abd al-Rahman: Abu Hurayrah narrated to me, saying: I used to call my mother to Islam while she was a polytheist. One day I called her, and she said words concerning the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) that I hated to hear. So I went to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) weeping and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I used to call my mother to Islam and she would refuse; today I called her and she said words concerning you that I hated to hear, so supplicate Allah to guide the mother of Abu Hurayrah!' The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'O Allah, guide the mother of Abu Hurayrah.' I left rejoicing at the supplication of the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). When I arrived and reached the door, it was bolted. My mother heard the sound of my footsteps and said: 'Stay where you are, O Abu Hurayrah!' And I heard the splashing of water. He said: She took a bath, put on her shift, and hastened without putting on her head-covering, then opened the door and said: 'O Abu Hurayrah, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger.' He said: So I returned to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), coming to him while weeping out of joy. He said: I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, rejoice, for Allah has answered your prayer and guided the mother of Abu Hurayrah!' He praised Allah, extolled Him, and spoke well. He said: I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, supplicate Allah to make me and my mother beloved to His believing servants, and to make them beloved to us.' He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'O Allah, make this little servant of Yours—meaning Abu Hurayrah and his mother—beloved to Your believing servants, and make the believers beloved to them.' Thus no believer has been created who hears of me or sees me but that he loves me.

'Abd al-Malik ibn Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to us: my father narrated to me, from my grandfather: Khalid ibn Yazid narrated to me: Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal narrated to me, from 'Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'A'ishah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Lampoon Quraysh, for indeed it is harder on them than being shot with arrows.' So he sent for Ibn Rawahah and said: 'Lampoon them.' He satirized them, but it did not completely satisfy. So he sent for Ka'b ibn Malik, then he sent for Hassan ibn Thabit. When he entered upon him, Hassan said: 'The time has come for you to send for this lion that lashes with its tail!' Then he stuck out his tongue and began flicking it, and said: 'By the One Who sent you with the truth, I shall surely tear them with my tongue as leather is torn!' The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Do not be hasty, for Abu Bakr is the most knowledgeable of Quraysh concerning their lineages—and I have lineage among them—until he isolates my lineage for you.' So Hassan went to him and returned, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, he has isolated your lineage for me; and by the One Who sent you with the truth, I will surely extract you from them just as a hair is extracted from dough.' 'A'ishah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying to Hassan: 'The Holy Spirit (Jibril) will continue to support you as long as you defend Allah and His Messenger.' And she said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: 'Hassan satirized them and cured [the believers] and healed himself.' Hassan said: 'You satirized Muhammad, so I responded on his behalf, and with Allah is the reward for that. You satirized Muhammad, righteous and godfearing, the Messenger of Allah whose character is fidelity. So indeed my father, his father, and my honor are a shield for the honor of Muhammad against you. May I lose my young daughter if you do not see our horses raising dust from the sides of Kada', pulling against their reins as they ascend, with thirsty spears upon their shoulders; our steeds continue galloping swiftly, while the women strike them with their veils. If you turn away from us, we shall perform 'Umrah, the conquest will occur, and the veil will be lifted; otherwise, endure the striking of a day in which Allah honors whomever He wills. And Allah said: "I have sent a servant who speaks the truth, with no obscurity about it." And Allah said: "I have prepared an army: they are the Ansar, whose objective is to meet [the foe]." Every day we have from Ma'add abuse, fighting, or satire. So whoever among you lampoons the Messenger of Allah, praises him, or supports him—it is not equal. And Jibril is the messenger of Allah among us, the Holy Spirit who has no equal.'

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Abdah narrated to us: Hisham ibn 'Urwah narrated to us, with this chain of transmission; she said: Hassan ibn Thabit asked permission of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) to satirize the polytheists. And he did not mention Abu Sufyan, and said in place of 'al-khamir' (fermented dough) 'al-'ajin' (dough).

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Yahya ibn Zakariyya informed us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: Hassan said: 'O Messenger of Allah, give me permission concerning Abu Sufyan.' He said: 'What about my kinship with him?' Hassan said: 'By the One Who honored you, I will surely extract you from them just as a hair is extracted from dough.' Then Hassan recited his poem: 'And indeed the pinnacle of glory among the family of Hashim is the sons of the daughter of Makhzum, while your father is a slave.'

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated it to us: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Shu'bah, in this chain of transmission, and he said: She said: 'He used to defend the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace),' and he did not mention 'A chaste, poised woman...'

Bishr ibn Khalid narrated to me: Muhammad—meaning Ibn Ja'far—informed us, from Shu'bah, from Sulayman, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, who said: I entered upon 'A'ishah while Hassan ibn Thabit was with her reciting poetry to her, eulogizing with verses of his, saying: 'A chaste, poised woman who is never suspected of doubt, and who wakes hungry from the flesh of unsuspecting women.' Thereupon 'A'ishah said to him: 'But you are not like that.' Masruq said: I said to her: 'Why do you permit him to enter upon you when Allah has said: {and he who took upon himself the greater portion of it from among them will have a great punishment}?' She said: 'And what punishment is more severe than blindness? Indeed, he used to defend or satirize on behalf of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).'
'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it to us: 'Abdah narrated to us, from Hisham, with this chain of transmission.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kuraib narrated to us; they said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, that Hassan ibn Thabit was among those who spoke much against 'A'ishah, so I reviled him. She said: 'O my nephew, leave him alone, for indeed he used to defend the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).'

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated it to me: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us; (H) and Abu Bakr ibn Nafi' narrated to me: Ghundar narrated to us; (H) and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far and 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us; all of them from Shu'bah, with this chain of transmission, the like of it.

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Adi—who is Ibn Thabit; he said: I heard al-Bara' ibn 'Azib say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying to Hassan ibn Thabit: 'Lampoon them—or satirize them—and Jibril is with you.'

'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to us: Abu al-Yaman informed us: Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri: Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed me that he heard Hassan ibn Thabit al-Ansari calling Abu Hurayrah as a witness: 'I adjure you by Allah, did you hear the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "O Hassan, reply on behalf of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace); O Allah, support him with the Holy Spirit"?' Abu Hurayrah said: 'Yes.'

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, Muhammad ibn Rafi', and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated it to us, from 'Abd al-Razzaq: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyab, that Hassan said in a circle in which Abu Hurayrah was present: 'I adjure you by Allah, O Abu Hurayrah, did you hear the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)...' and he mentioned the like of it.

'Amr al-Naqid, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Ibn Abi 'Umar all narrated to us from Sufyan; 'Amr said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id, from Abu Hurayrah, that 'Umar passed by Hassan while he was reciting poetry in the mosque, and gave him a disapproving look. Thereupon Hassan said: 'I used to recite poetry here when there was present one who was better than you!' Then he turned to Abu Hurayrah and said: 'I adjure you by Allah, did you hear the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "Reply on my behalf; O Allah, support him with the Holy Spirit"?' Abu Hurayrah said: 'O Allah, yes!'

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—and the wording is Qutaybah's: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sulayman ibn Mushir, from Kharashah ibn al-Hurr, who said: I was sitting in a circle in the mosque of Medina, and in it was an elderly man of fine appearance, namely 'Abdullah ibn Salam. He began narrating to them fine speech. When he stood up to leave, the people said: 'Whoever would be pleased to look at a man from the people of Paradise, let him look at this man.' I said: 'By Allah, I will surely follow him to know the place of his house.' So I followed him, and he proceeded until he almost left Medina, then entered his house. I asked permission to enter upon him, and he granted me permission and said: 'What is your need, O nephew?' I said to him: 'I heard the people say concerning you when you stood up: "Whoever would be pleased to look at a man from the people of Paradise, let him look at this man," so I desired to be with you.' He said: 'Allah knows best about the people of Paradise, and I will tell you why they said that. While I was asleep, a man came to me and said to me: "Get up!" He took me by the hand, and I went with him. Behold, there were wide pathways on my left. I started to take one of them, but he said to me: "Do not take them, for they are the pathways of the companions of the left." Behold, there were clear, prominent pathways on my right, so he said to me: "Take this way." Then he brought me to a mountain and said to me: "Climb!" Whenever I tried to climb, I would fall back on my rear, and I did that repeatedly. Then he took me until he brought me to a pillar whose top was in the sky and whose base was in the earth, and at its top was a ring. He said to me: "Climb onto this!" I said: "How can I climb this when its top is in the sky?" So he took my hand and tossed me up, and suddenly I was clinging to the ring. Then he struck the pillar and it collapsed, while I remained clinging to the ring until morning. I came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and recounted it to him, whereupon he said: "As for the pathways you saw on your left, they are the pathways of the companions of the left; as for the pathways you saw on your right, they are the pathways of the companions of the right; as for the mountain, it is the abode of the martyrs, and you will not attain it [martyrdom]; as for the pillar, it is the pillar of Islam; and as for the handhold/ring, it is the handhold of Islam, and you will never cease clinging to it until you die."'

Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Abbad ibn Jabalah ibn Abi Rawwad narrated to us: Harami ibn 'Umarah narrated to us: Qurrah ibn Khalid narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: Qays ibn 'Ubad said: I was in a gathering in which Sa'd ibn Malik and Ibn 'Umar were present, and 'Abdullah ibn Salam passed by. They said: 'This is a man from the people of Paradise.' So I stood up and said to him: 'They said such and such.' He said: 'Glory be to Allah! It is not proper for them to say that about which they have no knowledge. Rather, I saw [in a dream] as if a pillar was placed in a lush green meadow and erected in it; at its top was a handhold, and at its base was a minsaf—and minsaf is a servant. It was said to me: "Climb it!" So I climbed until I seized the handhold. I recounted it to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), whereupon the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "'Abdullah will die while firmly grasping the most trustworthy handhold."'
